sections.h2: Leelanau County Register of Deeds office
sections.html:
The office is at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, in Suttons Bay. Call 231-256-9682 or email rod@leelanau.gov. Documents received after 4:30 p.m. are held until the next business day, so a deed dropped off late in the afternoon is not recorded until the following morning.

This is the place where every deed, mortgage discharge and similar paper for Leelanau land is filed. Records here go back to 1863. The office records instruments that transfer or encumber real property. It cannot judge whether a document is legally sufficient or what its author intended. Michigan is a race-notice state, so papers are recorded in the order they are first presented, and first in time is first in line.

The whole county is the Leelanau Peninsula, a triangle of land that reaches into Lake Michigan from the western Lower Peninsula. Only 347 of its 2,532 square miles are land, because 86% of the area is water, and that shoreline and inland lake frontage shapes much of the housing market. The population was 22,301 at the 2020 census, up from 21,708 in 2010. The villages are Empire, Northport and Suttons Bay, and ten civil townships cover the rest. Every deed for any of this ground is filed in the Suttons Bay office, whether the parcel is a lake cottage, a farm or a village lot.

The office accepts only documents with original signatures, and it does not allow digital recording. The wet ink rule is deliberate, because it has stopped fraud attempts. Check these points before you bring a deed in:

  • A court document must be certified by the court. A true copy cannot be recorded, and the same applies to a death certificate.
  • Under MCL 565.201 each signer's name is printed, typed or stamped beneath the signature, and the signature is in black or dark blue ink.
  • The notary's name appears on the same page near the signature.
  • Each grantee's street address, or post office address, appears on a deed.
  • The drafter's name and business address appear on instruments signed after January 1, 1964.

The staff cannot supply forms or give legal help, and they do not run title searches. For drafting, ask an attorney or a title company.

A quick pre-check saves a second trip. Read the deed once more for the notary's name, the grantee's address and the drafter's name, and confirm the ink is black or dark blue. If anything is missing, the signers may need to fix it before the office can accept the paper, and a late fix can push back a closing.

State law sets recording at $30 for any document, whatever its length. The office takes cash, checks, debit cards and credit cards. One check can cover recording for several documents, along with transfer tax, a tax certificate and any copy fees.

ChargeAmount
Recording any document$30.00
Extra instrument on an assignment or discharge$3.00
Copy, in office or online$1.00 per page
Certified recorded document$5.00
Card convenience fee on $1 to $50$2.00
Card convenience fee above $50.012.95%

For a typical sale, plan on one check that covers the $30 recording fee, the transfer tax and any certified copy you want for your files. Bring the original signed deed, because a scan or photocopy will be turned away. If you pay by card, remember the convenience fee is added on top of the total.

Counties of this size levy 55 cents per $500 of value, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. Any leftover fraction counts as a whole $500 unit. The seller pays when the deed is filed, and stamps must be bought in the county that holds the land.

A few rules from the county's own guidance are worth knowing before closing. The deed has to show the total consideration. A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit may be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says so. If land straddles two counties, the price is divided between the parcels and each county is paid its share. An easement is taxable, and a foreclosure instrument carries county tax based on the stated sale price.

Exemptions listed in MCL 207.505 include transfers for under $100, instruments given as security, leases, land contracts that have not yet passed title, spousal conveyances creating a tenancy by the entireties and corrective quitclaims.

sections.h2: How do I search Leelanau County land records?
sections.html:
Use the county's Self Service site, the two public workstations in the Suttons Bay office, or the vault. Enter names last name first with no punctuation. A search needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year.

  • The free search shows index information only, and each image costs $1.00 per page.
  • Subscription passes run $5 for 15 minutes, $15 for a day, $200 a month and $1,100 for six months.
  • A parcel number search requires the county prefix 45 and the dashes, as in 45-000-000-000-00, and only documents that list the number turn up.
  • Online, only deed records are available before January 1, 1972. Older records of other kinds are searched in the office.
  • The historical grantor and grantee indexes went online in October 2025.

Try spelling variants, such as Richard, Rick and Dick, because names are indexed exactly as written on each document.

sections.h2: After a payoff, a death or a sheriff's sale
sections.html:
The office only records. It issues no replacement deed after any of these events, and your original deed stays the deed to the property.

  • After a mortgage payoff, the lender sends a discharge or satisfaction of mortgage. No new deed follows, because the deed was delivered when you bought.
  • When a co-owner dies, bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee. It shows that the deceased person no longer holds an interest.
  • A sheriff's deed is recorded when it is submitted after the auction closes. To redeem, contact the attorney named on the sheriff's deed.
  • If you have lost your deed, a recorded copy is available at the office, and copy fees apply.

If you are selling and one of these items is unfinished, get it recorded first. A buyer's title company will look for the discharge or the death certificate in the county index before it lets the sale close.

Subscribe to Fraud Notify, which costs nothing. It sends an email whenever a filing appears under a name you register, and the office has stopped several fraudulent attempts to list owners' property once owners were told.

If you see a neighbor's lot offered for sale, ask the owner. Also be wary of mail that looks official and charges for copies of your own deed. A 2016 Michigan law set rules for such mailings, and a copy from the office is $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 231-256-9682. The office is in Suttons Bay at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, and also takes questions by email at rod@leelanau.gov.

faqs.q: Does Leelanau County record deeds electronically?
faqs.a: No. The office requires original wet ink signatures and does not allow digital recording, to make deed fraud harder.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Leelanau County sale?
faqs.a: The county rate is 55 cents per $500 of value and the state rate is $3.75 per $500. The seller pays when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Will the office record a copy of a death certificate?
faqs.a: Only a certified one. A true copy cannot be recorded, and the office issues no new deed afterward because it only records.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my Leelanau County deed?
faqs.a: Go to the Suttons Bay office, call 231-256-9682 or use the Self Service website. Each page costs $1.00.
